Task: APRV-389.

## What this is

The daemon stopped `anchor-diverged` on 2026-09-19 while the working log carried the anchored record. The check proved two facts from two different reads: the byte digest from its own read of the file, and "is there a record at the anchored seq" from the tick's opening view. `approval log sync` rewrites `events.jsonl` under a running daemon, so a tick that opened inside that window held a stale view. Fact one passed on the new bytes, fact two failed on the old view, and the message asserted both a missing record and a prefix relation.

- One comparison over one triple (anchored copy, working bytes, a view of them) with a fourth internal answer, `moved`, for the two reads contradicting each other. A `moved` or `diverged` opening result re-reads the file once through the same verified read the tick uses (cache off) and compares again; a confirmed divergence still stops the daemon.
- A stop message quotes the chain comparison only where it agrees the chains parted; where records agree and bytes do not, it says the log was re-serialized, not re-chained.
- New daemon warning `anchor-reread`, one line, no stop. `log sync` is not made to refuse; the reasons are in `docs/dogfood-cutover.md` (sync is the repair for a dirty log, nothing tells a verb a daemon holds the log, and fixing the reader covers every writer of the file).
